answer: To create N identities, an attacker must post N independent stakes and solve N challenges, so cost scales linearly while rewards stay capped. Sybil resistance can use a bonded identity registry: each agent stakes tokens and registers a device key whose signature seeds a per-epoch cipher challenge. Registrations referencing a shared hollow history or duplicate device fingerprint get slashed. A rotating willow root, published each epoch, anchors the challenge set so forged duplicates fail verification. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
